findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, conventional, and interview-ready. Its rows, columns, visited, shapes, origin coordinates, neighbor coordinates, and offsets names expose the grid traversal and canonicalization directly, while the iterative stack avoids recursion-depth dependence without unnecessary abstraction.

The row-major scan selects the same translated anchor for congruent components, and four-neighbor traversal reaches exactly one maximal island while the global visited set prevents duplicate traversals. Subtracting that island's origin removes absolute position from every occupied cell. Equal frozen offset sets therefore mean exact translation equivalence, while any differing occupied coordinate, rotation, or reflection remains different because no such transform is applied.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 694, Python, and the native numDistinctIslands(grid) interface. The app-local solve(grid) adapter preserves rectangular binary-grid input, horizontal and vertical connectivity only, maximal islands, translation-only shape equivalence, distinct rotation and reflection, and the integer count of shape classes.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065588298 use the same row-major origins, global visited set, iterative four-neighbor traversal, relative-coordinate collection, frozenset shape representation, and final set cardinality. Their only structural differences are the required Solution.numDistinctIslands wrapper and Python typing dialect.

The unchanged authored workloads grow one dense island from 16 to 144 grid cells, forcing the protected algorithm to scan and traverse every cell exactly once. In a fresh real-test run, the exact protected source passed all eleven ordinary correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.01 and a 0.99x largest runtime ratio. A correct control that refloods the complete component from every land cell passed every ordinary and benchmark output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +1.07 and a 182.67x largest runtime ratio, distinguishing linear component visitation from quadratic repeated traversal.

The Approach accurately derives translation-invariant offsets, global single visitation, immutable shape hashing, exact equivalence, and the absence of rotation or reflection normalization. Its O(RC) time and O(RC) auxiliary-space claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The legacy document was replaced by a composition anchor and four modular Reference sections. The independent narrative preserves the binary matrix, maximal four-directional connectivity, water beyond all four edges, translation-only equivalence, distinct rotations and reflections, both exact source examples without invented explanations, and all four constraints. Two complete Markdown grid tables reproduce the information in the source's otherwise inaccessible example images.

Authenticated live Premium evidence verified the description, exactly two examples without explanations, all four constraints, and two source images that visualize the exact example matrices. The modular Reference is bound to source content hash b7f58045db88d81361d9d994d9ef94e56173dd6d870f69a5bfb67347fef797ee and every composed local section through source_fidelity.json; direct validation returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. Their exact matrices and outputs now appear first and in source order; the invented 3 by 3 singleton example was replaced by a smaller diagonal-separation trial outside the source sequence.

All ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden irregular component, translated L shapes, and reflected shapes were exposed, leaving no correctness behavior concealed in cases.json.

Contract boundaries cover one and fifty rows, one and fifty columns, both binary cell values, land touching grid boundaries, an all-water grid, and a one-cell island. The maximum row and column dimensions are each represented without turning an ordinary correctness case into a large performance workload.

Material behavior covers four-directional connectivity, diagonal separation, repeated translated shapes, multiple different shapes, rotation and reflection remaining distinct, irregular components, singleton equivalence, and zero-island output.

Expected results were checked by an independent union-find component oracle over all 74954 binary grids with one through four rows and columns and 500 deterministic random grids up to 15 by 15. Protected app and immutable native forms agreed throughout and on every authored case and benchmark, including the exact 1 by 50 and 50 by 1 boundary grids.

All eleven ordinary cases are visible. The unchanged dense 16, 64, and 144-cell workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 9x, and make the correct repeated-flood control fail only the scaling verdict.
